q: How do I calculate the emissions of an organic waste converter machine?
title: Organic waste converter emissions
short: Multiply the machine's electricity, from a sub-meter or rated power and hours, by 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh for FY 2024-25, and divide by kg of wet waste processed. Composting the output releases a little methane and N2O. Landfill emissions avoided are not deducted.
audience: Housing societies, campuses, hotels and canteens

ul: Electricity for the shredder, mixer and heater.
Additives such as sawdust or culture, as bought-in inputs.
Methane and N2O from the curing stage, from IPCC composting defaults if you calculate them.

p: Sending food waste to a converter instead of a landfill avoids methane, but that is an avoided emission. Report it separately, not as a reduction of your inventory.
Divide by kg of wet waste fed in, from the daily log, and report the kWh per kg so you can compare machines.

example.title: Worked example: housing society converter (one month, illustrative inputs)
lines: Total: 1,278 / 9,000 = 0.142 kg CO2 per kg of waste
example.note: Inputs are illustrative; use the sub-meter and waste log.

senseible: Senseible keeps waste manifests, transport invoices and treatment bills as evidence on the Scope 3 trail and reads electricity bills for on-site equipment into Scope 2. Avoided emissions are never subtracted from the inventory.
